Intellectual Conflict and the Foundations of Cultural Revival
This meaning shows, first, how useful the doctrine of compulsion was to Umayyad power.
Intellectual Conflict and the Foundations of Cultural Revival
It helped support the existence of the regime itself.
Intellectual Conflict and the Foundations of Cultural Revival
At the same time, it closed the door on any hope among Muslims that they might free themselves from Umayyad oppression.
Intellectual Conflict and the Foundations of Cultural Revival
If Umayyad rule came through an irresistible divine decree, then human beings had no power to resist God’s authority or free themselves from God’s decree.
Intellectual Conflict and the Foundations of Cultural Revival
They had no real choice over their actions.
Intellectual Conflict and the Foundations of Cultural Revival
Muslims therefore had to submit to Umayyad rule because, in doing so, they were supposedly submitting to God’s decree.
Intellectual Conflict and the Foundations of Cultural Revival
That was the political equation behind Umayyad reasoning.
Intellectual Conflict and the Foundations of Cultural Revival
But the same political and social meaning also tells us something about the Qadarite movement itself.
Intellectual Conflict and the Foundations of Cultural Revival
When Qadarite doctrine appeared as a developed theory through Maʿbad al-Juhanī, its call for human freedom became closely tied to opposition to Umayyad rule for two connected reasons.
Intellectual Conflict and the Foundations of Cultural Revival
First, the Umayyads shed Muslim blood and seized Muslim wealth.
Intellectual Conflict and the Foundations of Cultural Revival
Second, they claimed that this injustice had been imposed on people by God.
Intellectual Conflict and the Foundations of Cultural Revival
It would be more accurate to go even further.
Intellectual Conflict and the Foundations of Cultural Revival

The Qadarite call for freedom of human will and action carried, in its very meaning, a call for the oppressed to use that freedom of will and action to free themselves from the oppression of “these kings.”
Intellectual Conflict and the Foundations of Cultural Revival
The Qadarite doctrine therefore opened the door to hope.
Intellectual Conflict and the Foundations of Cultural Revival
Liberation was possible because human beings were not completely compelled by divine decree.
Intellectual Conflict and the Foundations of Cultural Revival
What do we learn from Ayyūb al-Sakhtiyānī’s debate with al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī over the question of human freedom?
Intellectual Conflict and the Foundations of Cultural Revival
Ayyūb was unable to persuade al-Ḥasan through argument, so in the end he threatened him with the Umayyads if he did not give up his Qadarite position.
Intellectual Conflict and the Foundations of Cultural Revival
Of course, Ayyūb had every right to debate al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī, or anyone else, over a doctrine with which he disagreed.
Intellectual Conflict and the Foundations of Cultural Revival
What goes beyond that right is replacing intellectual argument with a threat involving Umayyad power.
Intellectual Conflict and the Foundations of Cultural Revival
And this brings us directly to the heart of the matter.
Intellectual Conflict and the Foundations of Cultural Revival
Why threaten him specifically with the Umayyads?
Intellectual Conflict and the Foundations of Cultural Revival
Intellectual Conflict and the Foundations of Cultural Revival
The historical account itself gives it to us through both its wording and its meaning.
Intellectual Conflict and the Foundations of Cultural Revival
It is almost as if the report were saying directly that the Umayyads were watching for anyone who accepted Qadarite doctrine.
Intellectual Conflict and the Foundations of Cultural Revival
They were even prepared to punish people simply for believing it.
Intellectual Conflict and the Foundations of Cultural Revival
We can see this because Ayyūb did not merely ask al-Ḥasan to stop publicly preaching the doctrine.
Intellectual Conflict and the Foundations of Cultural Revival
He argued with him over the belief itself.
Intellectual Conflict and the Foundations of Cultural Revival
He wanted al-Ḥasan to abandon that belief completely.
Intellectual Conflict and the Foundations of Cultural Revival
When he could not persuade him through argument, he threatened him with the Umayyad authorities. According to the same historical account, al-Ḥasan then did in fact stop.
Intellectual Conflict and the Foundations of Cultural Revival
This shows that the Umayyads fought Qadarite doctrine relentlessly.
Intellectual Conflict and the Foundations of Cultural Revival
They fought it through intellectual argument, using people such as Ayyūb al-Sakhtiyānī and other supporters of compulsion.
Intellectual Conflict and the Foundations of Cultural Revival
They fought it through intimidation and terror.
Intellectual Conflict and the Foundations of Cultural Revival
And finally, they fought it by killing people such as Maʿbad al-Juhanī, ʿAmr al-Maqṣūṣ, Ghaylān al-Dimashqī and others.
Intellectual Conflict and the Foundations of Cultural Revival
As for why the Umayyads fought Qadarite doctrine, we have already explained this clearly, and we will return to it again elsewhere.
Intellectual Conflict and the Foundations of Cultural Revival
We now need to draw some conclusions from the letter that al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī wrote to ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Marwān after the caliph asked him about human freedom and divine compulsion.
Intellectual Conflict and the Foundations of Cultural Revival
We also need to consider al-Shahrastānī’s claim that the letter was not really written by al-Ḥasan but by Wāṣil ibn ʿAṭāʾ.
Intellectual Conflict and the Foundations of Cultural Revival
The fact that ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Marwān, while caliph, specifically asked al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī for his opinion on free choice and compulsion deserves serious attention.
Intellectual Conflict and the Foundations of Cultural Revival

We see it as an attempt by the Umayyad ruler to obtain an authoritative Islamic opinion from a major religious scholar whose views carried great weight among the educated people and intellectuals of Basra.
Intellectual Conflict and the Foundations of Cultural Revival
It seems to us that ʿAbd al-Malik hoped this opinion would condemn the Qadarites.
Intellectual Conflict and the Foundations of Cultural Revival
He could then use it as a religious weapon to defend the doctrine of divine decree and compulsion—in other words, to defend the ideology of Umayyad rule itself.
Intellectual Conflict and the Foundations of Cultural Revival
At the same time, he could use religion as a weapon against the Qadarite movement.
Intellectual Conflict and the Foundations of Cultural Revival
But how could ʿAbd al-Malik expect such a ruling from al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī himself, who was widely known at the time as one of the leading teachers of Qadarite thought in Basra?
Intellectual Conflict and the Foundations of Cultural Revival
We believe there are two reasons.
Intellectual Conflict and the Foundations of Cultural Revival
First, ʿAbd al-Malik would probably not have asked al-Ḥasan about such a sensitive issue unless he expected an answer that suited him.
Intellectual Conflict and the Foundations of Cultural Revival
Second, al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī was known to fear the power of the state.
Intellectual Conflict and the Foundations of Cultural Revival

Although he was then one of the leading teachers and advocates of Qadarite doctrine—perhaps its most important theoretical teacher—it was quite possible that fear of political authority would prevent him from stating his position openly.
Intellectual Conflict and the Foundations of Cultural Revival
Historical sources describe several situations that suggest this.
Intellectual Conflict and the Foundations of Cultural Revival

We have already mentioned the story told by Ayyūb al-Sakhtiyānī. He said that he argued with al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī about Qadarite doctrine several times but could not change his opinion until he frightened him with the threat of political authority. Al-Ḥasan then promised to abandon the view.
Intellectual Conflict and the Foundations of Cultural Revival
It appears that he did finally move away from it toward the end of his life.
Intellectual Conflict and the Foundations of Cultural Revival
There are other signs of his fear of the authorities.
Intellectual Conflict and the Foundations of Cultural Revival
Historians tell us that when Ibn al-Ashʿath rose against the Umayyads, al-Ḥasan urged people not to support him, even though al-Ḥasan himself strongly opposed Umayyad rule.
Intellectual Conflict and the Foundations of Cultural Revival
He took a similar position when Ibn al-Muhallab rebelled against the Umayyads in Basra. Again, al-Ḥasan called on people not to support the revolt.
Intellectual Conflict and the Foundations of Cultural Revival
It is difficult to explain these two positions except through his desire to protect himself from the punishment of the authorities.
Intellectual Conflict and the Foundations of Cultural Revival
Some have tried to use them as proof that al-Ḥasan was not really a Qadarite.
Intellectual Conflict and the Foundations of Cultural Revival
But this goes against the historical evidence.
Intellectual Conflict and the Foundations of Cultural Revival
Most of the reports describing his Qadarite views come from his own students, including Qatāda ibn Diʿāma al-Sadūsī, ʿAmr ibn ʿUbayd and Ayyūb al-Sakhtiyānī.
Intellectual Conflict and the Foundations of Cultural Revival

Al-Dhahabī also reports that al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī said that both good and evil occur within divine decree. In other words, neither good nor evil should be attributed to God in a completely unrestricted way.
Intellectual Conflict and the Foundations of Cultural Revival
Al-Sayyid al-Murtaḍā reports from Abū al-Jaʿd that he heard al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī say:
Intellectual Conflict and the Foundations of Cultural Revival
“Whoever claims that acts of disobedience come from God will come on the Day of Resurrection with a blackened face.”
Intellectual Conflict and the Foundations of Cultural Revival
And Dāwūd ibn Abī Hind reports hearing al-Ḥasan say:
Intellectual Conflict and the Foundations of Cultural Revival
“Everything is by decree and destiny except acts of disobedience.”
Intellectual Conflict and the Foundations of Cultural Revival
This last sentence appears word for word in the letter attributed to al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī and addressed to ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Marwān.
Intellectual Conflict and the Foundations of Cultural Revival
That supports the conclusion that the letter really was written by al-Ḥasan, not by Wāṣil ibn ʿAṭāʾ as al-Shahrastānī suggests.
Intellectual Conflict and the Foundations of Cultural Revival

Al-Shahrastānī gives no evidence for rejecting al-Ḥasan’s authorship except his own belief that al-Ḥasan would never have disagreed with the early Muslim authorities, who, as al-Shahrastānī puts it, held that divine decree, “both its good and its evil,” comes from God.
Intellectual Conflict and the Foundations of Cultural Revival
The claim that Wāṣil ibn ʿAṭāʾ wrote the letter is even stranger, because a simple historical calculation makes it impossible.
Intellectual Conflict and the Foundations of Cultural Revival
Wāṣil was born in 80 AH and died in 131 AH.
Intellectual Conflict and the Foundations of Cultural Revival
ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Marwān became caliph in 65 AH—fifteen years before Wāṣil was born.
Intellectual Conflict and the Foundations of Cultural Revival
ʿAbd al-Malik ruled for twenty years.
Intellectual Conflict and the Foundations of Cultural Revival
This means that Wāṣil was only about five years old when ʿAbd al-Malik died in 85 AH.
Intellectual Conflict and the Foundations of Cultural Revival
How could he possibly have written a letter to him?
Intellectual Conflict and the Foundations of Cultural Revival
There can be little doubt, then, that al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī held Qadarite views during an important and productive period of his intellectual and teaching career.
Intellectual Conflict and the Foundations of Cultural Revival
Nor do we doubt that he wrote the letter to ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Marwān.
Intellectual Conflict and the Foundations of Cultural Revival

The only serious objection comes from al-Shahrastānī, and he offers no convincing evidence for it. The historical evidence, as we have seen, actually destroys his suggestion that Wāṣil was the author.
Intellectual Conflict and the Foundations of Cultural Revival
Dr Iḥsān ʿAbbās was therefore right to say that there is more reason to attribute Qadarite views to al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī than to deny them completely.
Intellectual Conflict and the Foundations of Cultural Revival

The reports come from his own students, some of whom disliked the Qadarites and their doctrine. If they had been able to clear al-Ḥasan of the accusation, they would have done so. And if they had known of any reason for caution in attributing those views to him, they would have mentioned it.
Intellectual Conflict and the Foundations of Cultural Revival
That leaves one likely explanation for al-Ḥasan’s more hesitant positions, including his possible abandonment of Qadarite views late in life: his fear of persecution by the ruling authorities.
Intellectual Conflict and the Foundations of Cultural Revival
There is considerable evidence for this fear, some of which we have already mentioned.
Intellectual Conflict and the Foundations of Cultural Revival
If our discussion were not already so long, we could give more examples.
Intellectual Conflict and the Foundations of Cultural Revival
For now, one story reported by Ibn ʿAsākir will be enough.
Intellectual Conflict and the Foundations of Cultural Revival
He says that al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī once fled from al-Ḥajjāj’s soldiers and took refuge with Ḥabīb al-ʿAjamī, a Sufi and one of al-Ḥasan’s students.
Intellectual Conflict and the Foundations of Cultural Revival
Intellectual Conflict and the Foundations of Cultural Revival
“Abū Muḥammad, protect me from the police! They are right behind me!”
Intellectual Conflict and the Foundations of Cultural Revival
“Abū Saʿīd, I am ashamed for you. Do you not trust your Lord enough to pray to Him and ask Him to hide you from them?”
Intellectual Conflict and the Foundations of Cultural Revival
Some details in this story may be doubtful.
Intellectual Conflict and the Foundations of Cultural Revival
But the fact that the story was widely repeated tells us two things.
Intellectual Conflict and the Foundations of Cultural Revival
First, it adds to the other evidence showing how strongly al-Ḥasan feared the ruling authorities.
Intellectual Conflict and the Foundations of Cultural Revival
Second, it suggests that the Umayyad authorities were not satisfied simply because al-Ḥasan had warned people against supporting Ibn al-Ashʿath.
Intellectual Conflict and the Foundations of Cultural Revival
That was not enough while he continued to hold his position on human freedom.
Intellectual Conflict and the Foundations of Cultural Revival
The spread of Qadarite doctrine in Umayyad society posed a greater danger to the regime than al-Ḥasan’s personal support for the revolt of Ibn al-Ashʿath would have done.
Intellectual Conflict and the Foundations of Cultural Revival
Al-Ḥasan was a man whose words carried enormous influence among the people.
